premise_as_used_by_L01: Omaveloxolone: NRF2 dependence of its anti-inflammatory action
source_and_access: Probst 2015 (PMID 25897966), PMC4405374 Europe PMC XML; openFDA Skyclarys label set 2709e870-df3d-f30f-e063-6394a90aeda1 effective 2026-04-06
verbatim_locator: At low concentrations (≤ 25 nM), RTA 408 activated Nrf2 and suppressed nitric oxide and pro-inflammatory cytokine levels in interferon-γ-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophage cells. At higher concentrations, RTA 408 inhibited tumor cell growth (GI50 = 260 ± 74 nM). "Nrf2 activation is required for AIM-mediated NO suppression [3]. Consistent with this, we observed a decrease in nitric oxide synthase 2 (Nos2) protein levels in bardoxolone methyl-treated RAW 264.7 cells, which was attenuated when Nrf2 mRNA levels were reduced by siRNA (S1 Fig)." "AIMs have been shown to directly bind to cysteine 179 in IKKβ and inhibit NF-κB signaling" and "RTA 408 also inhibited TNFα-induced phosphorylation of IκBα in HeLa cells at concentrations similar to those of bardoxolone methyl". "RTA 408 dose-dependently decreased growth (Fig 3A) and inhibited colony formation (Fig 3B) in WT and Keap1 -/- MEFs." Cytokines measured in RAW264.7: "Nos2 (iNos), Ptgs2 (Cox2), Ccl2 (Mcp1), and Ccl5 (Rantes)"; IL-6/IL-1b strings: 0 hits. Label: "The mechanism by which omaveloxolone exerts its therapeutic effect in patients with Friedreich's ataxia is unknown." "Protein binding of omaveloxolone is 97%."
depth: Probst full text read (about 31k characters) ; label PK/MoA sections via openFDA JSON
verdict: SUPPORTED as stated; the decisive fact: the NRF2 siRNA control in that paper was done with bardoxolone methyl, not RTA 408; no published NRF2-loss control for omaveloxolone on IL-6/IL-1b was found in the searches run (not found is not absent)
what_changes: Omaveloxolone has a concentration window (NRF2-linked suppression at low nM in macrophages) below its IKKβ/NF-κB, JNK and growth-inhibitory window (hundreds of nM, tumour lines, a KEAP1-independent growth effect in Keap1-/- MEFs); 97% protein binding means the free concentration in serum-containing medium is not the nominal one. In vitro facts only: no dose, route or schedule is recommended

premise_as_used_by_L01: Monomethyl fumarate as a second NRF2 chemotype ("two chemotypes")
source_and_access: Sanchez-Sanz 2024 (PMID 39684792), PMC11642486 full text; Gillard 2015 (PMID 26004161, abstract); openFDA Bafiertam label a161f9d4-70f1-4097-957a-eafb35d3274f effective 2026-07-16
verbatim_locator: We found that DMF and CBD, but not MMF, activated the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway in neurons. "In neurons, DMF induced the translocation of Nrf2 to the nucleus at 30 µM compared to the vehicle (p = 0.0275)" ; "As for MMF, we did not observe the nuclear translocation of Nrf2 in neurons at the same concentrations of DMF (Figure 2B). Similarly, we did not observe Nrf2 activation by MMF in the microglial cells at any concentration (Figure 2B)." "only DMF and CBD, but not MMF, prevented the LPS-induced activation of the inflammatory pathway NF-kB in microglia". Gillard abstract: "DMF inhibited NF-κB-driven cytokine production and nuclear translocation of p65 and p52 in an Nrf2-independent manner. Equivalent doses of MMF and MEF did not affect NF-κB signaling." Label: "After oral administration, dimethyl fumarate undergoes rapid presystemic hydrolysis by esterases and is converted to its active metabolite, monomethyl fumarate (MMF)." and "MMF has been identified as a nicotinic acid receptor agonist in vitro."
depth: Sanchez-Sanz full text read (about 55k characters; murine microglia cell line, primary neurons; reading limited to Results/Discussion passages); Gillard abstract only; label sections
what_changes: MMF did not activate NRF2 in primary neurons or the microglial line in that source, while DMF did: DMF and MMF are not interchangeable (the card's "MMF (active moiety of DMF)" transfers evidence across a prodrug/metabolite pair). The moiety that reaches plasma and CSF (MMF) is the one without NRF2 activation in this source; DMF is the NRF2-active ex vivo form but is not the systemic moiety. One source, one lab, a cell line for microglia: other studies cited in it report partial MMF activity (so the finding is not universal)
